claims.claim: Changing language won't reliably get you under 2 seconds; the hosting plan and scaling decide latency, not the language
claims.about: .NET vs Node vs Go on Azure Functions Consumption
claims.measured: Container start-up: csharp-aspnet 785 ms, node-express 706 ms, node-fastify 593 ms, go-gin 293 ms, go-nethttp 238 ms
claims.why: The benchmark measured process start-up in Docker, not Azure Functions host, worker or scale-controller delays, so it can't show how much of the cold start the language accounts for.

claims.claim: With modern .NET on the isolated model, language worker start and startup code are a smaller share of cold start than people expect
claims.measured: csharp-aspnet start-up 785 ms vs go-nethttp 238 ms and node-express 706 ms
claims.why: There is no figure for the total Functions cold start, so the share can't be checked, even though .NET's measured start-up is under a second.
Only one modern ASP.NET Core configuration was measured.

claims.claim: A Node or Go function waits just as long for the scale controller to allocate an instance
claims.about: Node and Go on Azure Functions Consumption
claims.why: Platform scale-out delay isn't part of the measurements.

claims.claim: Turning on ReadyToRun and keeping startup code light improves .NET cold start
claims.why: No ReadyToRun or startup-variant builds were measured.

claims.claim: Native AOT .NET would cut startup time
claims.why: No Native AOT .NET server was benchmarked.
